methods: using sum and product of roots
statement: The roots of $x^{2}+px+q=0$ are $\\alpha$ and $\\beta$. Find, in terms of $p$ and $q$, the quadratic equation whose roots are $\\dfrac{\\alpha}{\\beta}$ and $\\dfrac{\\beta}{\\alpha}$.
solution: We have $\\alpha+\\beta=-p$ and $\\alpha\\beta=q$. The new roots are $r_{1}=\\alpha/\\beta$ and $r_{2}=\\beta/\\alpha$. Their sum is $r_{1}+r_{2}=\\dfrac{\\alpha^{2}+\\beta^{2}}{\\alpha\\beta}=\\dfrac{(\\alpha+\\beta)^{2}-2\\alpha\\beta}{\\alpha\\beta}=\\dfrac{p^{2}-2q}{q}$, and their product is $r_{1}r_{2}=1$. Hence the required quadratic is $x^{2}-\\dfrac{p^{2}-2q}{q}x+1=0$, or equivalently $qx^{2}-(p^{2}-2q)x+q=0$.
